title: The Whispered Roll
story: Two dice are rolled behind a curtain. A spy whispers: 'they show different numbers.'

phases.ask: P(at least one six | different numbers)?
P(first die is 6 | sum is 9)?

hints: Shrink the 6×6 grid to the cells that match the whisper. How many cells are left, and how many of those contain a 6?

title: The Ordered Draw
story: A pouch has {w} white and {b} black pearls. You draw 4 without replacement.

phases.ask: P(first two white, last two black)?

hints: Multiplication rule: P(E1E2E3E4) = P(E1)P(E2|E1)P(E3|E1E2)…
solution: Chain the conditional probabilities draw by draw.

title: Two Dragon Eggs
story: A nest has two eggs; each hatches a female or male dragon with probability 1/2, independently.

phases.ask: The OLDER egg is female. P(both female)?
You only learn that AT LEAST ONE is female. P(both female)?

hints: List the sample space {FF, FM, MF, MM} (older first). Which outcomes survive each piece of news?
solution: At least one female: {FF, FM, MF} → 1/3.
pattern: what exactly was observed changes the conditioning set

title: The Breeding Pouch
story: A magic pouch has {w} white and {b} black beads. Each drawn bead is returned along with {c} more of its colour.

phases.ask: P(the first three draws are all white)?
P(the second draw is white)?

hints: The pouch changes after each draw: update both the white count and the total.
For the second draw, condition on the first and simplify. Notice anything surprising?
solution: Chain rule with the updated counts.
pattern: Pólya urn: update counts; symmetry across draws

title: Late for Guard Duty
story: It rains tomorrow with probability {r}. On a rainy day the guard is late with probability {a}; otherwise with probability {c}.

phases.ask: P(the guard is late)?
He was late. P(it rained)?

hints: Draw the tree: weather first, then late or not.
Bayes: the share of 'late' probability that comes through the rain branch.

title: The Healer's Test
story: A plague affects {p} of the town. The healer's test detects it {s} of the time, but also flags {fp} of healthy people.

phases.ask: A villager tests positive. P(has the plague)?
P(has the plague | tests NEGATIVE)?

hints: Imagine 1000 villagers. How many are sick and test positive? How many are healthy and test positive?

title: Three Coins in the Box
story: A box holds a two-headed coin, a fair coin, and a coin that lands heads with probability {q}. One is picked at random and lands heads.

phases.ask: P(it was the two-headed coin)?

hints: Bayes with three hypotheses: weight each coin by P(heads | coin).

title: Gold in the Other Drawer
story: Chest A has gold in both drawers; chest B has gold in one and silver in the other. You open a random drawer of a random chest and see gold.

phases.ask: P(the other drawer of that chest also has gold)?

hints: Count the gold drawers you could have opened. How many of them belong to chest A?
solution: 3 equally likely gold drawers; 2 are in chest A → 2/3.
pattern: count equally likely observations, not objects

title: The Transfer Spell
story: Urn I: 3 white, 2 red. Urn II: 2 white, 3 red. A ball moves from I to II, then you draw from II.

phases.ask: P(the drawn ball is white)?
Given that it's white, P(the transferred ball was white)?

hints: Condition on the colour of the transferred ball.
pattern: condition on the hidden middle step

title: The Colour Trial
story: {m} of men and {w} of women in the realm are colour-blind; there are equal numbers of each. A colour-blind person is chosen.

phases.ask: P(the person is a man)?

hints: With equal priors, the 1/2s cancel.

title: Three Prisoners of the Keep
story: One of three prisoners A, B, C will be exiled, chosen at random. The jailer tells A one of the OTHERS who will stay free, picking at random if both are free. He says 'B'.

phases.ask: P(A is exiled | jailer said B)?
P(C is exiled | jailer said B)?

hints: Compute P(jailer says B | A exiled), P(jailer says B | C exiled), P(jailer says B | B exiled).
solution: Likelihoods ½, 1, 0 with priors ⅓ each → posteriors ⅓, ⅔, 0 (same logic as Monty Hall).
pattern: the informant's rule matters (Monty Hall logic)

title: The Balanced Academy
story: The academy has 3 first-year boys, 6 first-year girls and 5 second-year boys.

phases.ask: How many second-year girls are needed for 'sex' and 'year' to be independent for a randomly chosen student?

hints: Independence means P(boy | first-year) = P(boy | second-year).

title: The Bridge Circuit
story: A rune-circuit has gate 1 in series with a parallel pair of gates 2 and 3. Gates work independently with probabilities {p1}, {p2}, {p3}.

phases.ask: P(current flows)?

hints: Series → all must work (multiply). Parallel → at least one works (1 − all fail).

title: The Five Wards
story: A shield holds while at least {k} of its {n} wards work. Each ward works independently with probability {p}.

phases.ask: P(the shield holds)?

hints: The number of working wards is binomial. Which values count as a success?

title: Best of Seven
story: Your champion wins each bout with probability {p}, independently. The first to 4 wins takes the title.

phases.ask: P(your champion takes the title)?
P(the match goes the full 7 bouts)?

hints: Your champion wins in exactly k bouts if bout k is a win and exactly 3 of the first k−1 are wins.
Seven bouts happen exactly when the first six are split 3–3.

title: The Simultaneous Duel
story: You and the bandit fire at the same time each round. You hit with probability {a}, he hits with probability {b}. If both miss, you fire again.

phases.ask: P(you are the only one hit when the duel ends)?
P(the duel lasts exactly 3 rounds)?

hints: Rounds where both miss just restart the game. Condition on the round that ends it.
solution: P(you only hit, in the final round) = (1−a)b/(1 − (1−a)(1−b)).
pattern: restart → condition on the ending round

title: The Ferry Toll Game
story: You and the ferryman take turns rolling two dice, you first. You win as soon as you roll a sum of 8; he wins as soon as he rolls a 7.

phases.ask: P(you win)?

hints: Look at one full cycle (your roll, then his). Either someone wins in the cycle or it repeats.
solution: P(win) = P(win on your roll) / P(the cycle ends) = (5/36) / (1 − (31/36)(30/36)).
pattern: alternating trials → geometric series / cycle trick

title: The Gambler's Ledge
story: You hold {i} gold. Each bet wins 1 gold with probability {p} or loses 1. You stop when broke or at {N} gold.

phases.ask: P(you reach {N} gold)?

hints: Let P_i = P(success from i gold). Condition on the first bet: P_i = pP_{i+1} + qP_{i−1}.
Solve the recursion, or use the gambler's ruin formula.

title: The Queen's Secret
story: The queen carries a hidden curse with probability 1/2. If she does, each prince inherits it with probability 1/2. Her {k} princes are all free of it.

phases.ask: P(the queen carries the curse)?

hints: Likelihood of 'k clean princes' under each hypothesis?

title: The Withered Herb
story: Your neighbour waters your herb with probability {w}. Unwatered, it dies with probability {d1}; watered, with probability {d2}. You return to find it dead.

phases.ask: P(the herb survives), before you look?
P(the neighbour forgot | the herb died)?

hints: Tree: watered or not, then dies or not.

title: An Ace for Every Hand
story: A deck is dealt into 4 hands of 13.

phases.ask: P(each hand gets exactly one ace)?

hints: Track the aces one at a time: where does ace 2 go relative to ace 1? Then ace 3…
solution: Ace 2 avoids ace 1's hand: 39/51; ace 3: 26/50; ace 4: 13/49 → ≈ 0.105.

title: Which Coin?
story: You pick one of two coins at random; one lands heads with probability {p1}, the other with {p2}. Two flips: both heads.

phases.ask: P(you hold the {p2} coin)?
P(the third flip is heads)?

hints: Flips are independent GIVEN the coin, but not unconditionally.
Next-flip probability = posterior-weighted average.

title: The Bookmaker
story: A rider wins with probability 3/8.

phases.ask: What are the odds in favour of the rider, as a single number?

hints: Odds = P(E)/P(E^c).

title: The Friend's Two Cards
story: A friend draws two cards.

phases.ask: She says 'at least one is an ace'. P(both aces)?
She says 'one is the ace of spades'. P(both aces)?

hints: Count the hands that match each statement. The statements are not equally informative!
pattern: specific information conditions differently from vague information
